cur:catacombs-arles-trees.summary: Trees divide the front into niches where Christ, the apostles and the recipients of his miracles appear; among the scenes is the Wedding at Cana, where Christ touches the water jars with his rod. The leafy canopy evokes paradise as the setting of Christ's saving deeds.
facts: Commons notes that in the 18th century the sarcophagus was displayed in the archbishop's palace in Arles (FAN.92.00.2488).
It is carved from Proconnesian marble from the Sea of Marmara.

cur:manuscripts-valcavado-river-of-life.summary: In the heavenly city, drawn as tiers of arcades filled with saints, the figure enthroned in a mandorla at the top is the source of the river of the water of life, which flows down the page as a winding blue stream between trees on its banks. The paint is badly flaked, but the composition remains legible.
facts: The Valcavado Beatus was written and illuminated in 970 by the monk Oveco for Abbot Sempronius of Valcavado, in the reign of Ramiro III of León; it has 230 surviving leaves and 87 miniatures.
After the expulsion of the Jesuits under Charles III, the manuscript passed from their college of San Ambrosio in Valladolid to the University of Valladolid.
cur:manuscripts-valcavado-river-of-life.notes: The image is heavily worn; the central figure follows the text, 'proceeding out of the throne of God and of the Lamb'.

vam:O167864.summary: Engraved into a milky oval of chalcedony, three Magi approach in a row from the left, while at the right the Virgin sits enthroned with a halo, holding the Christ Child, who leans forward towards them; a star shines above. The figures are cut with simple, deep strokes, giving the tiny scene a solemn rhythm. Used as a seal, it would have impressed the image of the Epiphany into wax.
facts: The V&A describes the seal as provincial Byzantine and of uncertain date; it was given to the museum by W. Chapman in 1877.
The museum cites comparable gems published by W. F. Volbach (1923) for its dating.
vam:O167864.notes: Date given as 7th century in the V&A date field but described in the record as 'of an uncertain date'.
